Team — looping you in on ApexHealth's ask (deal APX-482). Ellen says they expect a sustained 3x in token throughput starting Nov and want a committed tranche with headroom and clarity on preemption. Procurement needs a mitigation plan this Thursday.

Options I see:
- Short tranche: reserve 8 GPUs dedicated (or equivalent slices) with conditional scale-up options; set explicit warm-up and prefix cache expectations.
- Cost/commit: they sign a 6–12 month reserved commitment at a discounted hourly for that tranche.
- Preemption: we can offer a soft-preempt policy (graceful slowdown + spillover to burst pool) or hard-preempt only for Force Majeure / SLA-exempt cases.

Vivek — can capacity speak to whether we can carve an 8-GPU tranche without impacting other committed deals? Ben/Laura — if we propose 8 GPUs with a 6-month commitment, what pricing band and credits make sense?

Sofia / team — quick ops read:

We can carve an 8-GPU tranche from the Dedicated pool for Nov—Mar if we tie it to a 6+ month reserved commitment and a defined traffic shape (the profile Ellen sent helps). Caveats:
- Impact: carving 8 GPUs will reduce our on-demand burst capacity in the N. Virginia region by ~12% during peak windows. That could increase latency risk for a handful of existing burst customers; I can quantify which deals are in the tail.
- Preemption policy: recommend \"tiered soft-preempt\" — during contention, Apex gets a 2-minute drain period, then we apply graceful token-rate throttling and route excess to the burst pool (best-effort). Hard preempt only if we exhaust burst pool and there is customer-level SLA enforcement. This preserves predictability while protecting higher-tier committed customers.
- Monitoring / SLOs: we’ll expose token/sec and p99 latency dashboards for Apex and set alert thresholds.

If sales wants a firmer SLA (no throttling), we need higher commitment (12 months) and additional unit credits to compensate other customers.

I can run a quick impact simulation tomorrow morning and attach a heatmap showing which deals see risk.

— Vivek
Head of Serving Runtime, Redwood Inference
